You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Weekly Strategy OPENAI

TEXT:
Fundamentals
OpenAI remains in a period of extremely rapid commercialization. At the end of March, the company disclosed that its monthly revenue had reached approximately
$2B . By September, market data showed that its annualized revenue run rate had reached at least
$40B . Enterprise growth has been particularly strong. OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar said enterprise revenue grew 32% from June to July, and enterprise and consumer businesses now each account for roughly half of total revenue.
The latest funding round was completed in March 2026 at a post-money valuation of
$852B . Meanwhile, the company remains in a period of heavy investment, with substantial spending on computing power, model training, and infrastructure. As it has yet to achieve stable profitability, its valuation should currently be assessed primarily using
P/S . OpenAI expects its long-term gross margin to improve as inference costs decline, but achieving positive cash flow will still take time.
In the short term, the fading IPO catalyst also warrants attention. Sam Altman has confirmed that OpenAI will not go public in 2026, meaning near-term price discovery in the Pre-IPO market will depend more heavily on operating data and changes in the valuation of the next funding round.
As OpenAI is not yet publicly listed,
OPENAI Pre-IPO perpetual futures/valuation contracts on major crypto trading platforms are used as a price proxy. The median quote across major platforms is approximately
$1400 , so this article uses
$1400 / an implied valuation of approximately $1.40T as a proxy for OpenAI's current market price.
Valuation
OpenAI does not currently generate stable net profit, so P/E is not calculated. Instead,
Forward P/S is used.

The $3.4B and $64B forecasts for 2026 and 2027 are based on previous HSBC estimates. The latest operating data already shows that OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate has reached at least $40B. Longer-term internal forecasts point to revenue of approximately $125B in 2029 and $174B in 2030.
Therefore, based on the current Pre-IPO market valuation of approximately
$1.40T , the market is effectively trading OpenAI at around
22× 2027 revenue, 11× 2029 revenue, and 8× 2030 revenue .
Technical levels and strategy
The OPENAI Pre-IPO price of approximately

On September 9, OPENAI perpetual futures reached a high of
1620.8 before falling significantly. On September 13, they dropped to a low of
1370 . The previous low on September 3 was approximately 1292, while the consolidation range before the early-September breakout was mainly around 1180–1230.
Bullish scenario
If OPENAI breaks back above
1500 , it would indicate that the market is beginning to absorb the valuation pressure caused by the recent IPO delay and AI safety controversies.
The first upside range to watch is
1570–1630 . A further breakout above the previous interim high of approximately 1630 would signal the start of a new round of price discovery, with
around 1700 as the next level to watch.
From a fundamentals perspective, enterprise revenue, Codex, Agent, and advertising monetization will need to continue driving upward revisions to revenue expectations.
Neutral scenario
If the price remains within the
1330–1500 range, it should be treated as consolidation at elevated levels.
Investors may consider building positions in batches near
1350–1400 . If the price approaches
1480–1500 again, it would be better to wait for breakout confirmation rather than chase the rally.
The current price of approximately 1400 is near the midpoint of this range and corresponds to roughly
22× 2027E P/S , meaning the price already reflects high expectations for future growth.
Bearish scenario
If OPENAI falls below
1330 , it would indicate further deterioration of the uptrend established in early September, with
1290–1300 as the next area to watch.
If 1290 also fails to hold, the price may retest the previous consolidation range at
1180–1230 .
A deeper risk is that the Pre-IPO valuation could converge toward the private funding valuation again. The current proxy valuation of approximately $1.40T still represents a premium of roughly 64% over the latest funding valuation of $852B. Therefore, if revenue expectations are revised downward, the IPO is delayed further, or pressure from AI capital expenditures worsens significantly, the Pre-IPO market itself has substantial room for valuation compression.
